title: Railway Bridge Project
description:
Hampshire County Council (HCC) own and maintain Havant Footbridge which crosses the railway at Havant in Hampshire. Whilst the footbridge is not part of the station infrastructure it is positioned within Network Rail (NR) land, with main span supports on the station platforms and access ramps within the forecourt and on NR non-operational land. Some sections are also within Havant Borough Council (HBC) land 

The footbridge was built in 1947 and provides the main public route over the railway. It connects the Civic Centre Campus, Havant College, and nearby large housing area of Leigh Park in the north to Havant Town Centre, Bus Station and Havant Park in the south. 

Deterioration of the footbridge has accelerated over recent years, and it is no longer deemed cost effective or practical to continue repairing it. In addition, the footbridge no longer meets uses needs. Therefore, the footbridge is to be removed, and a new one provided which meets current standards and provides access for all. 

Call off from Pagabo National Civils and Engineering Framework via Lot 2

title: Younger Adults' Supported Accommodation - Havant 4
description:
The Council wants to work with a support provider to deliver a Younger Adults Supported Accommodation in Havant for working age adults who have a Learning Disability, Physical Disability/Sensory Impairment, Mental Health Condition and/or Autistic Spectrum Conditions. Access to the services will be via a Care Act 2014 assessment.  

 

It is important for the Council to build relationships with a support provider that genuinely wants to work in partnership to actively explore, present and deliver service innovations that better meet the needs of clients, the service and the Council.   

The support provided will focus on developing greater self-reliance and independence and below is an indication of the range care and support that may be required by individuals living in the Younger Adults Supported Accommodation. 

 

Younger Adults Supported Accommodation (Havant 4) is made up of an initial 2 x 2 bedroom properties that will be used to accommodate 2 individuals with complex needs who benefit from having their own self contained accommodation. There may be future expansion of the Service if there is a requirement to support other individuals in the same area who also need similar individualised accommodation. 

 

The properties consist of an open plan living room/kitchen and dining area, 2 bedrooms upstairs and a bathroom upstairs. There is a larger bedroom which will be for the tenant and a smaller bedroom for the sleep in/staff accommodation. The properties have front and rear entrances and each have their own gardens. There are parking spaces allocated to each property. The properties are in the Havant area and are close to local amenities including local bus routes and a large area of park land. 

 

The Service requires support from an organisation which has extensive experience in supporting individuals with more complex needs including people with a range of learning disabilities.

title: Enhanced Menopause Support (Havant)
description:
The aim of this project is to improve the experience of menopause and the future health of women in the relevant age group, by offering a targeted, menopause-focused comprehensive health check, wellbeing consultation and onward referral to eligible women. This is a three year pilot project based in the target area of Havant, which has been identified as a priority area for the Hampshire County Council 'Your Future, Your Health' project.  

The PCN will be supported to offer women a by-invitation face to face consultation and assessment as follows: 

The service will be delivered over six sessions: 

Session one: 10 mins appointment for screening bloods as baseline NHS Health Check bloods + vitamin D, thyroid function tests, full blood count and haematinics  

Session two:  60 mins menopause health and wellbeing coach face to face appointment. Health check and holistic review to include: 

Measurements and risk scoring as standard NHS HC template 

Lifestyle questionnaire 

Menopause symptoms and bleeding questionnaire 

PHQ9 and GAD 

Dietary questionnaire 

Social and work situation 

Expectations questionnaire 

  

Session three: 30 minute appointment HRT Advanced Nurse Practitioner HRT discussion and plan.  

Session four: Personal care planning prescription for health and wellbeing and referral to any additional pathways of care already established e.g fitness classes. Following the MECC criteria the sessions will also ensure any new health issues or other concerns are planned for and signposted. 

Session five: 3 month HRT review with advanced nurse practitioner. 

Session six: 12 month review, evaluation and feedback

title: Work Out Your Money (WOYM) Financial Education for Adults
description: Work Out Your Money (WOYM) is a financial education initiative delivered by Citizen's Advice Havant, established in 2014. The objective is to change the community's perspective on money. Evidence shows people often only seek help when financial problems reach crisis point and that children learn money skills from their family, perpetuating poor money management across generations. Hampshire County Council wish to break this cycle so future generations have improved money skills. Debt and money is also often mentioned as a contributing factor in suicide, so this project aims to contribute to suicide prevention as per the Hampshire Suicide Prevention Plan. Similarly, addressing the mental wellbeing impact of cost of living pressures is a priority of the Hampshire Mental Wellbeing Strategy.

It is important to all parts of the Seetec Group that our Partners operate in ways which support our purpose, vision, mission and values. More information can be found https://seetec.co.uk/about/our-purpose-vision-mission-and-values/.

We're committed to providing opportunities and support to people from all walks of life and empowering them to shape their own futures. We provide tailored support to help participants progress in their journey, to deal with their barriers and move into sustainable employment.

Seetec require a provider who can deliver ESOL, Functional Skills, digital skills, employability, and employment enabling accreditations attached to employers with guaranteed interviews.  Training will be delivered across the Southwest and Uxbridge for unemployed learners looking to move back into work.  

ESOL and Functional Skills needs to include elements of employability to ensure that the focus remains on finding employment.  Overall objective is to improve learners' level of English to in turn, improve their employment prospects.  Learners are on programme for a limited time, so the teaching needs to be intensive to reduce the time taken to complete the qualification.  Learners will be various different nationalities, and the teaching needs to accommodate different levels of capability. 

Routeways should include sector-specific training, and the provider should have links to employers to offer guaranteed interviews at course completion to support participants into sustainable employment. 

The training interventions required include, but are not limited to:

ESOL and Functional Skills:
•	Entry Level 1 (E1) - Basic foundation skills.
•	Entry Level 2 (E2) - Slightly more advanced than E1.
•	Entry Level 3 (E3) - The highest Entry Level.
•	Level 1 (L1) - Equivalent to a GCSE grade D-G (3-1).
•	Level 2 (L2) - Equivalent to a GCSE grade A*-C (9-4).
Routeways into employment:
•	Level 2 Certificate in Spectator Safety.
•	Level 3 Certificate in Spectator Safety Supervision.
•	Level 3 Extended Certificate in Spectator Safety Supervision.
•	Level 4 Diploma in Spectator Safety Management.
Other training:
•	Non accredited employability and digital skills.
•	Any other courses or qualifications that would support customers into employment.

The delivery locations are:

Bath, Bristol, Wiltshire, Swindon, Plymouth, Weston Super Mare, Barnstaple, Exeter, Bridgwater, Torbay, Cornwall, Yeovil, Poole, Bournemouth, Weymouth, Southampton, Isle of Wight, Havant, Gosport and Uxbridge.

The provider must be able to deliver in all the above premises.

title: Drug and Alcohol Recovery Ambassadors and Communities
description:
This project is aimed to commission a provider with lived experience to lead on  the development and implementation of a Recovery Ambassador scheme in Havant, Fareham, and Gosport districts. 
- To develop a training programme for people with lived experience of drug and alcohol use to become recovery ambassadors within a range of community, workplace and treatment service settings. The programme should include a recognised/accredited qualification.  
- To deliver training and ongoing support to individuals, identifying personal goals and providing advice and guidance to achieve those goals.  
- To develop a network of Recovery Ambassadors to provide ongoing peer support and a collective voice for representation in local strategic planning and decision-making forums.  
- To undertake local engagement work to understand the needs and wants of local communities which will be used to help inform the development of local community recovery initiatives.  
- To engage with local community organisations, services, and employers to facilitate the development of opportunities for trained Recovery Ambassadors, depending on their individual goals/preferences.  
- To work with local research partners to design and support access to evaluation activities.  
- To work with Community Treatment providers to collaboratively build and develop community recovery initiatives that support long term recovery.

title: Connect 5 Training Community Offer
description:
The Connect 5 Training program aims to enhance people's capacity, capability, and confidence in having proactive and supportive conversations about mental health and wellbeing. Here's an overview of its scope:  

Understanding Mental Health and Wellbeing:  

Participants learn about mental health and wellbeing through specific public health models.  

They explore qualities and attitudes necessary for supporting and improving mental health.  

The focus is on recognizing the importance of self-help resources.  

Skills and Confidence Building:  

Connect 5 equips individuals with the skills and confidence to engage in mental wellbeing conversations.  

Participants learn how to talk with others about their mental health and wellbeing effectively.  

Local Services and Support:  

The training emphasizes understanding local mental health and wellbeing services.  

Participants learn how to guide people toward seeking support from these services.  

Principles of 'Making Every Contact Count':  

Connect 5 aligns with the principle of making the best use of frontline staff's skills and local contacts.  

It encourages proactive conversations in various contexts, such as workplaces and communities.  

The training consists of three modules, each approximately 3 hours long.   

Module 1 introduces participants to Connect 5, while Modules 2 and 3 build on the foundational knowledge, covering topics like suicide awareness and self-help tools.

The Community Wellbeing Worker service will provide short term, preventative support to these individuals, and will draw upon local community resources as required.
